info.cls_ename: Department of Foreign Languages and Literature

description.describe_ch: 本課程將引導學生進入西洋古典文學的領域，並希望能藉此帶領學生體驗此領域文學之奧妙，發掘文學閱讀的樂趣，進而培養文學欣賞的能力。本課程的學習將有助於培養學生在未來閱讀英、美、及歐洲文學作品時的理解力及較深刻的剖析能力。
description.describe_eh: This course is to introduce to students of English the field of classical western literature, covering ancient years to 100 BC. By reading the literary works of this early period, students will know the powerful imagination and creativity of the authors before Renaissance as well as the development of earlier western thought. Moreover, they will find some pleasure from their reading to further their appreciation and analysis of key literary works in the wide body of British, American, and European literature.

targets.describe_ch: 具備歐美文學的基礎知識
targets.describe_en: To be equipped with basic knowledge of European and American literature

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new:
Students’ final grades will be determined by five key components of their academic performance: attendance, participation, quizzes, and exams. Further descriptions of each category are as follows:
 
Attendance (0%)
Attendance is mandatory. The instructor will take attendance at the beginning of each class from September 9th to December 30th. It is the students’ responsibility to sign in for their attendance; otherwise, they may be marked as absent.
Each student is allowed up to 3 unpenalized absences during the semester. Additional absences beyond these may be excused under the following conditions:
 
(i) If a student must miss one or more classes for a legitimate reason, such as attending a conference, a competition, or an interview, the absence(s) can be excused provided the student submits an official document verifying the reason either in advance or afterward.
(ii) If a student misses one or more classes due to an emergency or unanticipated event, the absence(s) can be excused provided the student submits an official document verifying the occurrence afterward.
Excluding the additional absences that can be excused under the conditions stated above, students will receive a 2-point deduction from their final overall score for each unexcused absence from the 4th to the 5th, in addition to the initial 3 unpenalized absences. If a student accumulates 6 or more unexcused absences overall, they will fail the course automatically. Furthermore, if a student has 6 or more absences overall, including the initial 3 unpenalized absences, regardless of their legitimacy, the student’s final course grade will be the original grade lowered by two letters (e.g. A+ → A- ; B+ → B- ; C+ → C- ; and so on.).
Students will be marked as absent even if they are present under the following conditions:
(i)  They arrive to class more than 10 minutes late without a legitimate reason.
(ii) They leave the class early without obtaining the instructor’s permission before the start of the class.
(iii) They become distracted in class by engaging in other activities, such as using their mobile devices (especially their cellphones!), chatting, sleeping, doing homework, or preparing for a quiz or an exam for the next class, etc.
Students with perfect attendance (no absence, lateness, or tardiness) will be awarded with a 2-point bonus added to theirfinal overall score.
  • Grading Scale
A+   90–100     A   85–89     A-   80–84
B+   77–79       B   73–76      B-   70–72
C+   67–69       C   63–66      C-   60–62
D     40–59
E     1–39
X     0
  • See FCU Grading Scale at:
https://myfcu.fcu.edu.tw/main/S6800/S680004_Out_Download.aspx?originfilename=(%E5%85%AC%E5%91%8A)%E9%80%A2%E7%94%B2%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%B8%E5%AD%B8%E7%94%9F%E5%AD%B8%E6%A5%AD%E6%88%90%E7%B8%BE%E8%A9%95%E9%87%8F%E8%A6%81%E9%BB%9E_%E4%BF%AE%E8%A8%82%E5%85%A8%E6%96%87_1130329.pdf&newfilename=4c20cf706cf749e8963448d426a337ac_2_1.pdf.
 
Participation (10%)
Students are encouraged to speak up, ask questions, and actively participate in group discussions and in-class activities. Nevertheless, tardiness and in-class disruptions, such as sleeping in class, using cellphones, or any behaviors that interrupt class, will negatively impact their participation grade.
 
Oral Presentation (15%)
Groups of 4 to 5 students will give a 20-to-25-minute oral presentation on the texts we read in this course. Each week, one group will present during the first hour of the class (after the quiz, if there is one), from September 24th to December 24th, with a total of 12 groups presenting through the semester. All oral presentations should include three parts: (1) an introduction to the assigned texts; (2) a close reading of a selected character and/or passage of interest; and (3) a Q & A section where the presenters and the audience can engage in discussions on the presentation and other related questions.Students have complete freedom in how they organize and deliver their presentations, but the bottom line is that everyone in the group must participate and present.
 
Quizzes (35%)
There will be 7 quizzes this semester, each worth 5% of students’ final grade. Each quiz will consist of 10 multiple-choice questions, with a maximum score of 100 points. These quizzes will test students’ knowledge of names, terms, plots, and other details from the texts we read in this course.
 
Exams (40%)
There will be a midterm exam and a final exam, worth of 20% and 20% of your final grade, respectively. Each exam will consist of multiple-choice questions and matching questions, with a maximum score of 120 points. These exams will assess your overall understanding of the texts we read in this course.
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno: A lack of knowledge regarding academic honesty is not a valid excuse for any violation. Questions related to course assignments and academic honesty should be directed to the instructor. Students with learning disabilities may require accommodations. Please speak with me during the first week of class so that we can work out a plan together.
